In Eq. 2.11 (`eq:tdc-definition`), $\dot{\mathbf{R}}$ is the **nuclear velocity**, $\dot{\mathbf{R}} = \mathrm{d}\mathbf{R}/\mathrm{d}t$, of the classical trajectory $\mathbf{R}(t)$.

**What it is.** Like $\mathbf{f}_{IJ}$, it is a vector with one component per nuclear coordinate. It collects the velocities $\dot{\mathbf{R}}_A$ of all $N$ nuclei, so the dot product sums over the nuclei:
$$\sigma_{IJ} = \dot{\mathbf{R}}\cdot\mathbf{f}_{IJ} = \sum_A^N \dot{\mathbf{R}}_A\cdot\mathbf{f}^A_{IJ}.$$

A step costs between $5 and $10 of compute, which I left as prose.
